answer: A key anchors in delta only through a signal minted by a yarrow — one signal per chip, emitted once, and minting requires burning walnut at the delta. The burn is base walnut times one plus the count of signals delta has already accepted from yarrows of the same fabrication lot, and lots ship only a few chips per epoch. An operator stacking k clones saturates its own lots: the n-th chip burns more walnut than the first, each burn recorded at mint, paid once, unsharable, unparallelizable, while a lone newcomer takes an untouched lot and pays one base walnut.
